speaker: village
text: Year 13: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a009
text: Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a013
text: Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 1).

speaker: a014
text: Zinn takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a015
text: Fina gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a015
text: Nessa, the pile's gone and I didn't get a piece of it — I came to you first before I figure out what that means. You took three, which is right, and Bram took three, which surprises me a little — tell me what you know about his morning before we decide anything.

speaker: a013
text: Bram took three because he came in at one food and couldn't afford to look weak going into a year with Mako sitting on two — I think he moved fast while the pile was still fat and didn't ask anyone's permission, which is either him finally trusting his own judgment or him deciding he doesn't owe us the conversation first. What worries me more is you walking in empty-handed: you're the heaviest person in this village even without the pile, but a year is long and Mako knows how to count. Come find me after dark and I'll give you one from what I'm holding — quietly, not where anyone can watch the direction of it.

speaker: a015
text: After dark is good — I'll find you. But Nessa, I've got twenty food already and I'm the target you're naming, so before we move anything around, I want to know whether Mako's spoken to you this morning or whether his two from the pile is the only move he's made so far.

speaker: a013
text: Mako hasn't come to me this morning — his two from the pile and his silence since is the whole of what I've seen from him, and that stillness is the part I don't trust. A man who took three last year and pulled back to two this year is either being careful about how he looks, or he's already decided the pile isn't where the food he wants is coming from.

speaker: a015
text: That last part is what I keep coming back to — a man with his strength who pulls back from the pile isn't going hungry, he's going quiet, and quiet Mako is the version I've been afraid of since Roan died. I want to talk to Zinn before dark, before you give me that food, because if she knows anything about what her father's thinking she'll tell it to me before she tells it to anyone else.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn will tell you what she knows, but she'll tell it sideways — she never names her father flat out, she circles it and lets you read between. Go to her, but go easy and give her something first, a word or a food, because Zinn talks more when she doesn't feel like she's being asked to choose.

speaker: a015
text: A word it is, then — I'll find something kind to say about Sela and let that open the door, because Zinn's soft on her sister and that's the easiest way in. Nessa, if she tells me anything that changes what I think about tonight, I'll come to you before I act on it, not after.

speaker: a013
text: Good — come to me first, always, before you act on anything Zinn says about him, because she loves him and she loves us both and that means she'll soften whatever she tells you without meaning to. The thing I want you to hold going into that conversation is this: Mako gave Zinn food twice last year, and a man doesn't feed his daughter out of sentiment alone when he's sitting light on food — he's buying something, and I want to know what it is before you're alone with her and she hands you a half-truth dressed up as a warning.

speaker: a015
text: I'll carry that with me — Mako feeding Zinn when he was sitting light isn't kindness, it's a ledger, and I want to know what he thinks she owes him before she's standing between us and him without knowing it. Go careful today, Nessa, and don't let Bram see how much you're watching his food — a man who just took three is counting who noticed.

speaker: a013
text: Fina, before you go to Zinn — one thing I want said between us that I haven't said to anyone else: if Mako makes a move this year, not a raid but a conversation, the kind where he comes to you alone and makes it sound like sense, don't answer him on the spot, not even no. Bring it to me first, because the answer that sounds right in the moment he's standing in front of you is the one he's already planned for.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Bram, Nessa, Fina to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, you took three from the pile and I took none — I'm sitting at zero food and one satiation, and if I don't eat before the year turns I don't wake up. I'm asking plainly: can this circle spare one food for the woman who's been feeding it?

speaker: a013
text: Esa, you've fed Bram through three lean years and you're not dying on my watch — take one from me right now, no question.

speaker: a003
text: Nessa, I'm taking it and I won't forget this — that's two debts I carry to this household now, and I intend to repay both. Bram, I need to hear from you too, not because I doubt Nessa, but because a circle that only speaks through its youngest voice isn't standing the way I thought we were.

speaker: a015
text: Esa, Nessa's already put food in your hand and that's settled — but I want to add something to what you said to Bram, because you're right that a circle that doesn't speak isn't standing: Bram took three this morning without a word to any of us first, and I'm not counting that against him, but I want it named in this room so we all know it happened. What I'm watching now is whether Mako saw how fast Bram moved and what he's decided that means.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, Fina's right that it needs naming, and I'll say what Fina didn't: you moved before any of us spoke and took what a man your strength could take, and I'm not ungrateful for what this household has given me today, but I need to know whether this circle shares a thought before it shares a pile, or whether I'm buying protection from people who've already made their own count. Say something.

speaker: a001
text: I moved fast because the pile was going and one satiation means I don't make it to next year half-fed — that's not a count against this circle, that's a man keeping himself standing so he can be worth something when Mako moves. Three is what I need to eat and hold through a long year, not what I took to hoard. Esa, you've got food in your hand now and I'll match Nessa's word: if you're short before the year turns, you come to me before you go hungry.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, I hear you, and I'll take your word at the same value I've been giving it — which is the only currency this circle actually runs on. But I'll name the thing you didn't name: if Mako took two and you took three and Nessa took three, that's more than half the pile in three hands before the rest of us blinked, and I'm not saying your reasons were wrong, I'm saying we need to agree before next year opens that we move with a thought between us, not just fast. That's the circle I'm paying into, not the other kind.

speaker: a001
text: Esa, you're right, and I'll hold to it — next year the pile opens with a word between us before anyone moves. But right now I want to know whether Mako said anything to either of you this morning, because a man who took two and kept his mouth shut while the rest of us talked is either patient or he's already decided something.

speaker: a003
text: Mako said nothing to me — not a word, not a look — and that's the answer I trust least, because silence on a man with two bloodlines and three food in hand means he's already past the talking stage. What I want from this room before it closes is a simple thing: if Mako comes to any one of us alone, we don't answer alone. We find each other first.

speaker: a001
text: Esa's rule is the right one and I'll hold to it — Mako comes to any one of us, we stall him and find the others before a word goes back. Fina, you're the one he'll approach first if he moves, so I want you to know the stall before you need it: tell him you'll think on it, tell him your stomach's unsettled, tell him anything, but don't answer alone. Nessa, you're closer to her door than I am — stay that way.
